info.title: SKU.io — Reconcile a Supplier Statement
info.description: Reconcile what a supplier says you owe them against SKU.io's accounts payable, and trace the bank payments in between. Takes the supplier's statement (an emailed QuickBooks/Xero statement, a PDF, or pasted text) plus the bank lines paid to that supplier, compares them with the supplier's bills, vendor credits and payments in SKU.io, and explains every difference: bills a payment settled but SKU.io still shows open, payments recorded twice, credits applied in SKU.io that the supplier has not applied, bill totals that differ from the supplier's invoice (missing freight, a mis-linked line), and documents one side has that the other lacks. Proposes the fix for each and, under the caller's approval policy, applies the SKU.io side: unapply or apply credits, record a supplier payment, remove a duplicate payment. Use for "does our statement from X match", "why does SKU.io say we owe X more than they do", or a regular supplier account reconciliation.

get.summary: Resolve the supplier named on the statement to its id. (A bare GET /api/suppliers 405s.)

parameters.name: filter[search]
parameters.description: Supplier name or email from the statement.

schema.description: Supplier name or email from the statement.

get.summary: SKU.io's own statement for the supplier, in tenant currency. view=open_item (default) gives open_items[] (doc_type, id, number, supplier_invoice_number, purchase_order, date, due_date, total, total_paid, credits_applied, deposits_applied, outstanding_balance, status), credits[] (open, unapplied credits with `available`), deposits[] and totals{open, credits, deposits, net_payable}. view=activity gives opening/closing balance and lines[] (date, type, reference, debit, credit, running_balance; type invoice | bill | payment | credit_applied | credit_unapplied | deposit_applied | deposit_unapplied) for a date range.

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description: ISO date, on or after date_from. Required when view=activity.

schema.description: ISO date, on or after date_from. Required when view=activity.

get.summary: Every bill for the supplier, paid ones included (the statement only lists open ones). Rows carry supplier_invoice_number, purchase_invoice_date, calculated_total + tax_total (the gross total; there is no single total field), total_paid, outstanding_balance, status, payments[] and applied_vendor_credits[] (each with its allocation id and vendor_credit number).

parameters.name: filter[status]
parameters.description: unpaid, partially_paid or paid. Omit for all.

schema.description: unpaid, partially_paid or paid. Omit for all.

parameters.name: filter[purchase_invoice_date.after]
parameters.description: ISO date, to bound the window.

schema.description: ISO date, to bound the window.

parameters.name: filter[search]
parameters.description: Supplier invoice number, PO number or total. Pair with search_columns=supplier_invoice_number for an exact number lookup.

schema.description: Supplier invoice number, PO number or total. Pair with search_columns=supplier_invoice_number for an exact number lookup.

get.summary: One bill with its lines, payments and applied credits, to compare with the supplier's invoice line by line.

parameters.name: purchaseInvoice
parameters.description: Purchase invoice id (not the supplier's invoice number).

schema.description: Purchase invoice id (not the supplier's invoice number).

get.summary: Payments recorded on one bill: id, amount, payment_date, payment_type, external_reference. An external_reference with a provider prefix (xero:…, qbo:…) means the payment was imported from the accounting system rather than recorded in SKU.io.

delete.summary: Remove one payment from a bill. Only for a proven duplicate; see the guardrails.

get.summary: The supplier's OPEN vendor credits only (remaining amount above zero). A fully applied credit is not listed; find those through each bill's applied_vendor_credits[].

delete.summary: Take a credit back off a bill. Reopens the credit, raises the bill's outstanding balance, and shows as credit_unapplied on the activity statement. The allocation id is applied_vendor_credits[].id on the bill.

post.summary: Apply one or more open credits to one bill in a single all-or-nothing call.

allocated_at.description: ISO date the credit was used, normally the payment date.

notes.description: Why (max 1000 chars), e.g. the bank reference of the payment that used it.

get.summary: The supplier's open bills oldest-due first, with `total` spread across them greedily. A starting point only; it is not how the supplier applied the money.
Supplier payments recorded in SKU.io (one payment across several bills), newest first.

post.summary: Record money that already left the bank as one payment across one or more bills. Credits cannot be part of it: apply them to the bills first, then pay the net. Each allocation must not exceed the bill's outstanding balance; all bills must share a currency.

payment_date.description: The date the bank line cleared, ISO.

payment_type_id.description: From list-payment-types. Omitted, it falls back to "Cash".

external_reference.description: The bank line's own reference (ACH/wire number), so the payment can be traced.

allocations.description: Each { purchase_invoice_id, amount } (or bill_id for a non-PO bill).

get.summary: Resolve payment_type_id by name (e.g. "Bank Transfer", "ACH"). Don't invent the id.

delete.summary: Reverse a supplier payment recorded in SKU.io (and its accounting-system batch, if it was pushed).
